title: Katharine Abraham, an economics professor, was chatting with…

sents.en: Katharine Abraham, an economics professor, was chatting with her hairdresser (理发师) about retirement plans.
sents.cn: 经济学教授凯瑟琳∙亚伯拉罕（KatharineAbraham）正在和她的理发师聊退休计划。

sents.en: The economist said she plans to continue working because she wants to.
sents.cn: 这位经济学家说，她打算继续工作是因为她想工作。

sents.en: The hairdresser agreed but for a different reason: She needs the money.
sents.cn: 理发师表示认同，但理由不同：她需要钱。

sents.en: Both scenarios (情况) are contributing to a big increase in the number of people in the US working into their 70s.
sents.cn: 这两种情形都促使美国工作到70多岁的人数大幅增加。

sents.en: Over the past 20 years, the share of Americans working in their 70s has risen from less than 10% to nearly 15%.
sents.cn: 过去20年里，美国70多岁仍在工作的人的比例已从不到10%升至接近15%。

sents.en: In addition to people being healthier and living much longer, economists say that a combination of financial considerations such as years of slow rise in real wages and a shift away from traditional pensions in the private sector are some of the reasons people delay retirement.
sents.cn: 除了人们更健康、寿命更长之外，经济学家表示，实际工资多年缓慢上涨、私营部门逐渐放弃传统养老金等财务因素的综合作用，也是人们推迟退休的部分原因。

sents.en: The decline of manufacturing and the increase in the number of people working in less labor-intensive occupations also has contributed to the trend, says Abraham, who researches work and retirement decisions of older Americans.
sents.cn: 研究美国老年人工作与退休决策的亚伯拉罕说，制造业的衰退，以及从事劳动密集度较低职业的人数增加，也推动了这一趋势。

sents.en: ·Which matters more depends on what your history up until that point has been in the type of work you're doing,· Abraham says.
sents.cn: 亚伯拉罕说："哪一种因素更重要，取决于你在此前所从事的那类工作中有着怎样的经历。"

sents.en: The overall trend is hitting Americans of all different levels of educational attainment, although the percentages vary by category.
sents.cn: 这一总体趋势正冲击着受教育程度各不相同的美国人群，尽管各类别所占比例有所不同。

sents.en: The share of Americans with bachelor's degrees who were working into their 70s reached nearly 20% in 2018.
sents.cn: 2018年，拥有学士学位、工作到70多岁的美国人比例接近20%。

sents.en: For those with a high school degree or less, the proportion of those working in their 70s had risen to around 10%, while those with some college education were in the middle at around 15%.
sents.cn: 对于那些高中学历及以下的人，工作到70多岁的比例已升至约10%；而那些接受过部分大学教育的人则处于中间，约为15%。

sents.en: Martin Neil Baily, an economist who is leading a research project on retirement security, notes that quitting a career can lead to feelings of isolation and loneliness, particularly for men.
sents.cn: 主导一项退休保障研究项目的经济学家马丁∙尼尔∙贝利（MartinNeilBaily）指出，退出职业生涯会让人产生孤立和孤独感，对男性尤其如此。

sents.en: He suggests that many college-educated workers are choosing to stay in the labor force more for social benefits than for financial reasons.
sents.cn: 他认为，许多受过大学教育的劳动者选择留在劳动力市场，更多是出于社交方面的益处，而非财务原因。

sents.en: They're also more likely to be in professional occupations where they tend to enjoy their work more.
sents.cn: 他们也更可能从事专业职业，而在这类职业中他们往往更享受自己的工作。

sents.en: Workers in more physical jobs, meanwhile, may be more likely to look forward to retiring, Baily says, suggesting those who stay on are more likely doing so for financial reasons.
sents.cn: 贝利说，与此同时，从事更偏体力工作的人可能更期盼退休，这表明那些继续工作的人更可能是出于财务原因。
